questions.takeaway: Data encrypted on the client before upload stays unreadable even when access controls are set wrong.

read.text: Encrypted data stays unreadable even if access is left open.

questions.stem: A pharmacy chain worries that a misconfigured permission could one day expose prescription files it stores on AWS. Which measure keeps the files unreadable even if access is opened by mistake?

options.text: Compressing the files into one archive before each upload
options.why: Compressed files are smaller, but anyone who reaches them through a bad permission can still unpack and read them.

options.text: Copying the files across several Availability Zones
options.why: Copies across AZs protect against an outage, but each copy would be just as readable if exposed.

options.text: Scanning the files for malware on its own systems first
options.why: A malware scan checks the files are safe to store, but it leaves them readable to anyone who reaches them.

options.text: Encrypting the files on its own systems before upload
options.why: Files encrypted before upload stay unreadable to anyone without the key, even if access is left open.

questions.takeaway: An EC2-hosted database trades AWS-run upkeep for fine control over the OS and engine.

read.text: You get fine control, but patching, scaling and the OS are yours while AWS runs the hardware.

questions.stem: What does a customer gain by hosting a database on Amazon EC2 instead of on a managed database service?

options.text: Full control of the OS and engine settings
options.why: Running the engine on EC2 gives the customer fine control over the OS and setup, in exchange for the upkeep.

options.text: Automatic patching of the database engine
options.why: Engine patching is something a managed service handles, while on EC2 the customer applies patches itself.
Hosting on EC2 means the customer provisions and sizes its own instances for the database.

options.text: AWS ownership of who can read the data
options.why: Access to stored data stays the customer's choice under any hosting model, so AWS never owns it.

questions.takeaway: AWS Backup replaces scattered per-service backup plans with one central place for policies and restore points.

read.text: Separate disk and database backup plans overlap and confuse, so it unifies them in one dashboard.

questions.stem: A logistics company set up data protection one service at a time for its EBS volumes, EFS file systems, RDS databases and DynamoDB tables, and the separate plans now overlap. It wants one dashboard to set protection rules and see restore points for all of them. Which service fits?

options.why: AWS Backup brings backups for EBS, EFS, RDS, DynamoDB and more under one set of policies and one view.
Data Lifecycle Manager automates EBS snapshots only, so it cannot cover the file systems and databases too.
Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers for fast recovery, not central backup policies across these services.
Storage Gateway links on-premises systems to AWS storage and does not manage backups of these AWS resources.

questions.takeaway: To refuse specific senders for a whole subnet, use a network ACL deny rule, since security groups only allow.

read.text: Network ACLs work at the subnet level, are stateless, and support both allow and deny rules.

questions.stem: An insurance broker must stop one known hostile range of IP addresses from reaching any instance in a subnet, while other traffic keeps flowing. Which VPC control can block that range with a deny rule?

options.why: A network ACL guards the whole subnet edge and accepts deny rules, so it can turn away that one range.
A security group takes allow rules only, so it cannot name a range to refuse.
A route table decides where traffic is sent, not which senders are refused at the subnet edge.
An internet gateway connects the VPC to the internet and has no rules for turning senders away.

questions.takeaway: When compliance, proximity and services are equal, the different rates each Region charges decide the choice.

read.text: AWS pricing is transparent and granular, yet each Region has its own rates.

questions.stem: A game studio faces no legal limits on where its data is stored, and its players are spread evenly across the world. Two AWS Regions both offer every service it needs. What should guide its choice between those two Regions?

options.why: Distance does vary by Region, but with players spread evenly across the world, neither Region is nearer to most of them.

options.text: The rates charged in each Region
options.why: Each Region sets its own prices, so with compliance, proximity and services equal, cost is what remains to compare.
Services do differ between Regions, but both of these already offer everything the studio needs, so this cannot decide.

options.text: The data laws each Region follows
options.why: Each Region follows local law, but the studio has no legal limits on where its data lives, so law does not separate them.

questions.takeaway: A variable expense follows consumption, as an AWS bill does, while a fixed expense stays the same whatever the usage.

read.text: Fixed costs are paid up front for data centers and servers whether or not you use them, while variable costs on AWS follow only what you actually consume.

questions.stem: In cloud economics, which description fits a variable expense?

options.text: A cost paid once upfront for hardware, whatever the later usage
options.why: A one-time upfront hardware payment is a fixed expense, since it stays the same however little is used.

options.text: A cost that stays the same each month regardless of activity
options.why: A cost that never changes with activity is the definition of a fixed expense.

options.text: A cost that rises and falls with the resources consumed
options.why: A variable expense follows consumption, which is how an AWS bill behaves from month to month.

options.text: A cost agreed in exchange for committing to a long term
options.why: A long-term commitment locks in spending ahead of time, rather than letting it follow actual use.

questions.takeaway: Common questions and troubleshooting answers, including on security, are found in the AWS Knowledge Center.

read.text: Knowledge Center: Q&A, troubleshooting.

questions.stem: Which AWS resource is the place to look up answers to common security questions in a question-and-answer format?

options.why: Knowledge Center gathers questions and answers plus troubleshooting help, including on security topics.
Security Center is the main AWS cloud security site, an overview rather than a question-and-answer collection.
AWS Artifact gives access to AWS compliance reports and agreements, not answers to common questions.
Customer Compliance Center offers customer stories, whitepapers and checklists rather than a Q&A collection.

questions.takeaway: The customer owns the EBS data lifecycle, from scheduling snapshots to deleting the ones it no longer needs.

read.text: Your data is your job under shared responsibility, so you provision, move, deprovision and back up volumes.

questions.stem: An online bookstore runs its order system on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon EBS volumes. It wants regular snapshots of those volumes, with the old snapshots removed over time. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, how is this work split?

options.text: AWS schedules the snapshots, and the bookstore deletes the old ones
options.why: Scheduling backups is part of looking after the data, so it falls to the bookstore and not to AWS.

options.text: The bookstore schedules the snapshots and deletes the old ones
options.why: The data on the volumes is the customer's, so the bookstore both plans the snapshots and prunes old ones to control cost.

options.text: AWS schedules the snapshots and deletes the old ones
options.why: AWS runs the hardware behind EBS, but backing up the data on the volumes and cleaning up old copies is the bookstore's job.

options.text: The bookstore schedules the snapshots, and AWS deletes the old ones
options.why: Pruning old snapshots to keep costs down is also the bookstore's task, so AWS does not remove them on its behalf.

questions.takeaway: Provisioning for today and scaling with real demand, instead of a forecast, is the stop guessing capacity benefit.

read.text: On AWS you provision for today and scale with real demand in minutes, not weeks or months, keeping performance optimal without over- or under-provisioning.

questions.stem: A concert ticket seller has no reliable forecast of how many buyers its new site will attract. It wants to start with modest resources and add more as real traffic arrives. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud addresses this?

options.why: Going global is about reaching other countries quickly, while the seller's problem is an unknown amount of traffic.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.why: Economies of scale lower prices through bulk buying, which leaves the sizing problem unsolved.
Speed and agility covers fast experiments by teams, while the seller needs capacity that tracks real demand.
Starting with what is needed today and scaling with actual demand removes the need for a forecast.

questions.takeaway: Cost optimization searches every service in a solution, not only the compute layer where many teams start.

read.text: Solutions usually combine services, so look for savings across the design (here EC2, RDS in a VPC, and S3).

questions.stem: A ticket-booking startup runs an application that combines Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS and Amazon S3. It has already trimmed its EC2 instances and asks where else it should search to lower its monthly AWS spend. Which statement answers that question in line with AWS guidance?

options.text: Savings may also sit in the database and storage layers
options.why: The design combines several services, so the RDS and S3 parts of the bill deserve the same search as the instances.

options.text: Many teams begin their search for savings with EC2
options.why: It is true that EC2 is a common first stop, but the startup has done that step and asks where to look next.

options.text: Data coming in from the internet carries no transfer fee
options.why: Inbound transfer is indeed free, but that fact names no part of the design where the startup could still save.

options.text: Unit prices can drop as overall usage keeps growing
options.why: Volume pricing is a real AWS principle, but it explains a falling rate rather than where to search for savings.

questions.takeaway: A managed service takes day-to-day server upkeep off the payroll once it is configured.

read.text: After you configure one, AWS keeps it running with no server management on your part.

questions.stem: An online bookstore spends many staff hours patching and restarting the message queue servers it runs itself. It wants to cut that recurring operations cost while its systems keep pulling orders from a queue as they do today. Which service fits?

options.why: SQS is a managed queue that AWS keeps running once configured, so the staff hours go away and orders still wait in a queue.
SNS is managed too, but it pushes messages to subscribers instead of holding them in a queue, so the order flow would change.
Moving the queue servers to EC2 instances leaves the bookstore patching and restarting them, so the operations cost stays.
A Lightsail server bundle is still a server the bookstore looks after, so the patching hours do not shrink.

questions.takeaway: AWS runs and secures the software and hardware behind security groups, while the customer writes each group's traffic rules.

read.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, setting up network ACLs and security groups for your subnets and resources is your job.

questions.stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which security group task falls to a customer that runs Amazon EC2 instances?

options.text: Choosing which inbound traffic each group allows
options.why: The customer decides which senders and ports a security group admits, which is security in the cloud.

options.text: Running the filtering software that enforces group rules
options.why: The software that enforces the rules is part of the service AWS operates, so it is security of the cloud.

options.text: Patching the operating system inside each instance
options.why: Patching the guest operating system is a customer job, but it is not a security group task as the stem asks.

options.text: Securing the physical hosts that run the instances
options.why: The hosts behind EC2 are AWS hardware, so protecting them falls under security of the cloud.

questions.takeaway: Pay-as-you-go pricing charges only for the resources consumed, with nothing paid upfront and no long-term contract.

read.text: You pay only for the AWS resources you consume, just as staff earn wages only for hours on shift.

questions.stem: A photo-printing service runs its order site on AWS. Its bill rises in the holiday season and falls in quiet months, at the same rate per resource throughout, with nothing prepaid and no contract signed. Which pricing approach does this bill reflect?

options.why: Commitment discounts need a usage commitment over a term, and the service has signed no contract.
Volume discounts lower the rate as usage grows, while this service pays the same rate in its busy months.
Paying only for what is consumed, with nothing upfront and no contract, is pay-as-you-go pricing.
Reserved Instances trade a term commitment for a discount, which the service has not made.

questions.takeaway: Elastic Beanstalk turns uploaded code into a scaled, load-balanced environment that the customer still controls.

read.text: Give this fully managed service code and settings, and it builds the EC2 setup, scaling, load balancing and health checks.

questions.stem: A county library's small IT team wants to deploy its web catalog by handing AWS its code and settings. AWS should then build the load balancing, scaling and health checks, while the team keeps control of every resource. Which service fits?

options.why: Elastic Beanstalk takes code and settings and builds the scaling, load balancing and health checks, while the team keeps control.
CloudFormation builds resources from templates the team writes, rather than taking app code and deploying it.
Lightsail sells simple server bundles at a set price, and it does not build an auto-scaled environment from code.
Auto Scaling adjusts instance counts but leaves the deployment, load balancing and health checks to the team.

questions.takeaway: AWS re:Post is the community question-and-answer site that hosts the AWS Knowledge Center.

read.text: AWS re:Post: community Q&A that hosts the AWS Knowledge Center of FAQ articles and videos.

questions.stem: Which AWS resource is a community question-and-answer site that also hosts the AWS Knowledge Center?

options.why: re:Post is the AWS community question-and-answer site, and the Knowledge Center's articles and videos live on it.
The Trust and Safety Center is where suspected abuse is reported, rather than a general question-and-answer site.
Prescriptive Guidance publishes expert guides and patterns, rather than community questions and answers.
The Support Center is where customers open cases with AWS Support, rather than a community forum.

questions.takeaway: Many Linux instances sharing one self-scaling file system points to Amazon EFS.

read.text: Thousands of concurrent NFS connections let many EC2 instances share files, and every change is visible to all of them at once, with no manual syncing.

questions.stem: A hotel group runs a booking app on a fleet of Linux EC2 instances that must all read and write the same files at the same time. Storage should grow and shrink by itself as files change. Which service fits?

options.why: An EBS volume attaches to one instance at a time and keeps a fixed size until someone changes it.
Instance store serves only the instance on its host and loses its data on a stop, so the fleet cannot share it.
S3 stores objects in buckets, and it is no shared Linux file system that instances mount and edit in place.
EFS is an elastic NFS file system that many Linux instances share at once, growing and shrinking with the files.

questions.takeaway: AWS Control Tower sets up and polices a governed multi-account environment with templated accounts and controls.

read.text: Account Factory: stamps out each new account from one configurable template.

questions.stem: A restaurant franchise group is giving each of its locations a separate AWS environment and wants governance built in from the start. Which capabilities does AWS Control Tower provide for this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Offering staff a catalog of approved resources to launch
options.why: A curated catalog of approved resources is what AWS Service Catalog offers, not Control Tower.

options.text: Creating each new account from one configurable template
options.why: Control Tower's Account Factory builds every new account from one template, so each location starts out the same way.

options.text: Tracking software licenses brought over from on premises
options.why: Tracking and controlling software licenses is the job of AWS License Manager rather than Control Tower.

options.text: Sharing vetted networking and security setups for reuse
options.why: Sharing approved baseline networking and security setups is part of AWS Service Catalog, which governs resources rather than accounts.

options.text: Blocking launches that would go past a license limit
options.why: Usage caps and blocked launches that keep licenses compliant come from AWS License Manager, not Control Tower.

options.text: Enforcing rules that block or fix nonconforming resources
options.why: Control Tower's guardrails stop deployments that break the rules and catch noncompliant accounts and resources.

questions.takeaway: Letting AWS run the physical work of a data center frees money and staff time for the business itself.

read.text: A data center keeps costing money after it is built, for utilities, maintenance, and racking, stacking and powering servers.

questions.stem: An architecture firm's IT staff spend much of each week racking servers, replacing failed power supplies and paying cooling bills. The firm wants that time and money spent on client projects instead. On AWS, which change removes these ongoing costs?

options.text: Lower unit prices that come from AWS buying hardware in bulk
options.why: Bulk buying lowers the price of each resource, but the firm's cost is the ongoing work of running its facility.

options.text: A bill that follows usage in place of an upfront hardware purchase
options.why: A usage-based bill replaces the upfront purchase, while the firm's issue is the daily upkeep of its servers.

options.text: Deploying the firm's applications to other countries in a few clicks
options.why: Reaching other countries quickly does nothing about the racking, repairs and cooling the firm pays for.

options.text: AWS taking over the physical running of the server facilities
options.why: AWS takes over racking, powering and cooling servers, which frees the firm's staff and budget for clients.

questions.takeaway: For a large online move into AWS storage with throttling, scheduling and task reports, choose AWS DataSync.

read.text: It handles instances, encryption and network tuning, and lets you throttle, schedule, filter and report on tasks.

questions.stem: A film archive must copy a very large set of files from its on-premises storage into Amazon S3 over its network. It wants the transfer throttled during work hours, scheduled at night and reported on after each task. Which service fits?

options.why: DataSync automates large online moves into AWS storage and lets the archive throttle, schedule and report on each task.
Direct Connect only supplies a dedicated network path, so a service like DataSync must still manage and report on the move.
Transfer Family runs managed file exchanges over protocols such as SFTP, rather than throttled, scheduled bulk copies from storage.
The Snow Family ships data offline on devices, which misses the archive's plan to send data over its network.

questions.takeaway: Rebuilding an app with new code and cloud-built features is refactoring, which pays off big but costs the most upfront effort.

read.text: New code and cloud-built features, driven by a strong need for features, scale or performance

questions.stem: A music streaming startup has a monolithic application that lacks the features, scale and performance it now needs. It accepts the highest upfront planning and staff effort to rebuild with new code and cloud-built features. Which migration strategy is this?

options.why: Refactoring rebuilds an application with new code and cloud-built features, paying the highest upfront effort for features, scale or performance.
Replatform adds only a few cloud optimizations without new code, which is too little for the startup's needs.
Rehost moves the application unchanged, so the monolith would keep its current limits.
Relocate moves existing VMs or containers to a cloud host as they are, with no rebuild of the application.

questions.takeaway: Least privilege means granting only the access a person or system needs for its task.

read.text: Least privilege is the guiding principle: allow only what a person or system needs.

questions.stem: An accounting firm's interns need to view reports kept in one Amazon S3 bucket. Following the principle of least privilege, what access should the firm grant them?

options.text: Read access to the reports bucket only
options.why: Least privilege grants only what the task needs, which here is reading the one bucket that holds the reports.

options.text: Read access to every bucket in the account
options.why: Reading every bucket reaches data the interns have no need for, so it grants more than viewing the reports requires.

options.text: Read and write access to the reports bucket
options.why: Write access lets interns change reports they only need to view, so it grants more than the task requires.

options.text: Access to list the account's bucket names
options.why: Listing bucket names does not let the interns open any report, so this access falls short of the task.

questions.takeaway: Ready-made recommendations drawn from each customer's history point to Amazon Personalize rather than a custom model.

read.text: Per-customer picks from historical data

questions.stem: An online grocery store wants each shopper's home page to suggest products based on that shopper's past orders. The team has no machine learning specialists and wants to avoid building or training a model itself. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Personalize is a ready-made service that turns each customer's history into tailored product picks.
SageMaker AI could host a custom recommender, but the team would have to build and train that model itself.
Comprehend analyzes the meaning and sentiment of text, which does not produce per-shopper product picks.
Kendra answers search queries over company content, but it does not recommend products from order history.

questions.takeaway: Amazon VPC is the service for a private, isolated network in AWS whose address ranges and subnets you define.

read.text: Amazon VPC gives you a logically isolated part of the AWS Cloud with a virtual network you design.

questions.stem: Which AWS service gives a company its own private, isolated network inside the AWS Cloud, with address ranges and subnets that the company chooses?

options.why: Amazon VPC creates an isolated network in the AWS Cloud whose ranges and subnets the customer defines.
Direct Connect is a private line into AWS, not the isolated network that resources live in.
Transit Gateway connects existing networks through a hub rather than creating an isolated network.
PrivateLink gives private access to services from a network, but it does not create the network itself.

questions.takeaway: IP Hash routing keeps each client IP address on one server, unlike Round Robin or Least Connections.

read.text: IP Hash: routing that pins each client IP address to one server.

questions.stem: Which load balancing routing method keeps sending each client to the same server, based on the network address the client connects from?

options.why: IP Hash pins each client IP address to one server, so that client always lands on the same one.
Round Robin cycles through servers in order, so one client's requests move between servers.
Least Connections picks the server with the fewest open connections, whoever the client is.
Least Response Time picks the fastest server at that moment, not a fixed server per client.

questions.takeaway: Designing architecture and the target state for moving workloads, led by roles such as cloud architects, is the AWS CAF Platform perspective.

read.text: Patterns for new cloud solutions and moving on-premises workloads; architectural models, detailed target state

questions.stem: A cloud architect at a furniture maker designs the architectural models and a detailed target state for moving its on-premises workloads to AWS. Which AWS CAF perspective does this work fall under?

options.why: The Platform perspective provides patterns and architectural models for moving workloads, and cloud architects are its typical role.
Operations sets routines for running and recovering workloads once they live in the cloud, rather than designing the target state.
The Security perspective chooses and implements security controls, rather than designing the overall architecture.
People handles change management, skills and staffing, which differs from designing architectural models.

questions.takeaway: An AWS Config rule states a required setting and keeps reporting which resources pass or fail it.

read.text: Config rule: a standard Config checks resources against.

questions.stem: A hotel group's policy says every storage volume in its account must be encrypted. It wants each volume that breaks this policy to be reported as noncompliant, now and whenever settings change later. What should it set up?

options.why: A Config rule is the standard Config checks each volume against, and it keeps reporting pass or fail as settings change.
An alarm reacts to a metric crossing a threshold, and encryption is a resource setting rather than a performance number.
A framework maps resources to a standard for gathering audit evidence, but the per-volume setting check comes from Config.
An Artifact report covers how AWS itself was audited, which says nothing about the hotel group's own volumes.

questions.takeaway: The AWS Health Dashboard is the account-specific view of AWS events affecting your resources, with fix advice.

read.text: The dashboard adds updates and timely fix advice to manage service health at scale.

questions.stem: During a service disruption, an online crafts marketplace wants a view specific to its own account of the AWS events affecting its resources, with updates and timely advice on fixes. Which tool fits?

options.why: The AWS Health Dashboard gives an account-specific view of events with updates and fix advice during a disruption.
CloudWatch dashboards show metrics the team picked, but they carry no AWS notices or fix advice about service events.
Trusted Advisor checks the account against best practices rather than reporting AWS events during a disruption.
Control Tower's dashboard summarizes account compliance, which says nothing about AWS events hitting the marketplace.

questions.takeaway: Dedicated Hosts give a whole server and control over placement, at a higher price, for compliance or licensing needs.

read.text: A Dedicated Host gives control over instance placement and resource allocation, which helps with compliance and with licensing such as Windows or SQL Server.

questions.stem: Which statements describe Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts? (Select TWO.)

options.text: They give one customer a whole physical server
options.why: A Dedicated Host is an entire physical server reserved for a single customer.

options.text: They let the customer control where instances are placed
options.why: Control over instance placement helps with compliance rules and with server-bound software licenses.

options.text: They cost less than Reserved Instances for the same use
options.why: Dedicated Hosts cost more than Reserved Instances, so they are used only when server control is needed.

options.text: They isolate instances while AWS picks the physical server
options.why: Isolation with AWS choosing the server describes Dedicated Instances, not Dedicated Hosts.

options.text: They run on spare capacity that AWS can reclaim at any time
options.why: Reclaimable spare capacity describes Spot Instances, not a server held for one customer.

questions.takeaway: The AWS shared responsibility model divides security work, with AWS securing the cloud and customers securing what they run in it.

read.text: AWS owns security of the cloud, including all physical security, and the customer owns security in the cloud.

questions.stem: A craft brewery moving to AWS asks which security tasks AWS takes on and which stay with the brewery. Which AWS concept sets out this division?

options.why: The Well-Architected Framework guides how to design sound workloads, rather than dividing security tasks between AWS and the brewery.
The shared responsibility model splits security into AWS's share, of the cloud, and the brewery's share, in the cloud.
AWS CAF organizes guidance for migrating to AWS, rather than assigning security tasks to AWS or to the brewery.
The global infrastructure is the Regions, AZs and data centers AWS runs, not a split of security duties.

questions.takeaway: Application code calls AWS through the AWS SDK for its language.

read.text: The AWS Software Development Kit (AWS SDK) lets code in languages like Python, C++, Java and .NET call AWS, with AWS docs and sample code.

questions.stem: Which tool lets an application written in a language such as Java, Python or .NET call AWS services from its own code?

options.why: The AWS SDK gives language libraries so application code can call AWS directly.
The AWS CLI takes typed commands in a terminal rather than calls made from inside application code.
The console is a web interface for people, not a library that application code can call.
CloudShell is a browser terminal with the AWS CLI, not a library built into an application.

questions.takeaway: Real-time ingestion that several applications read at once points to Kinesis Data Streams.

read.text: Serverless, real time, terabytes from apps, streams and sensors; several apps can read one stream at once; on-demand mode provisions and scales itself

questions.stem: A ride-sharing company sends location updates from its drivers' phones without a break, day and night. Several separate applications, including pricing and dispatch, must each read the same incoming updates the moment they arrive. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests data in real time and lets several applications read one stream at the same time.
Firehose delivers data in near real time to a destination, which suits loading storage rather than live readers.
SQS holds messages until one consumer handles each, so several apps cannot each read the full stream.
EMR processes big data on Apache frameworks after it lands, and it does not ingest a live stream for many readers.

questions.takeaway: Shield Standard gives customers free, automatic DDoS defense on services such as CloudFront.

read.text: AWS Shield Standard: free, automatic, real-time defense against common DDoS attacks, built into ELB, CloudFront and Route 53.

questions.stem: A small travel agency serves its booking site through Amazon CloudFront. It pays for no security subscriptions and has written no firewall rules of its own. Which statements describe the protection the site already has? (Select TWO.)

options.text: AWS Shield Standard comes at no extra charge
options.why: Shield Standard is free, so the agency has it on its CloudFront site without paying for any subscription.

options.text: AWS Shield Standard works without any setup
options.why: Shield Standard is automatic and built into CloudFront, so the agency's site is covered although its team configured nothing.

options.text: AWS Shield Advanced gives in-depth attack diagnostics
options.why: Shield Advanced does offer in-depth diagnostics, but it is a paid tier, and the agency pays for no subscriptions.

options.text: AWS Shield Advanced mitigates sophisticated attacks
options.why: Shield Advanced does handle sophisticated DDoS attacks, but only for customers who pay for it, which the agency does not.

options.text: AWS WAF refuses requests from IPs in a web ACL
options.why: AWS WAF does block IP addresses listed in a web ACL, but the agency has written no such rules, so this is not in place.

questions.takeaway: For ongoing automated best-practice checks on security and cost, pick AWS Trusted Advisor.

read.text: AWS Trusted Advisor is that expert, automated: it runs live best-practice checks across your account.

questions.stem: An online travel agency wants an automated service that keeps checking its account against AWS best practices and points out open security gaps and wasted spending. Which service fits?

options.why: Trusted Advisor runs ongoing best-practice checks across the account and flags security gaps and savings.
Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and gives no advice on wasted spending.
Access Analyzer refines IAM permissions, a narrow security task that leaves cost and other best practices unchecked.
AWS Health reports AWS events affecting the agency's resources, rather than checking its setup against best practices.

questions.takeaway: ElastiCache keeps Redis OSS, Valkey and Memcached tools working, and its serverless option sizes the cache by itself.

read.text: Fully managed caching compatible with Redis OSS, Valkey and Memcached, so existing tools keep working.

questions.stem: A travel booking site will add Amazon ElastiCache beside its Amazon RDS database. Its developers want to keep the caching client code they already wrote for their current self-run cache, and the team wants no manual work adding or removing cache nodes as bookings rise and fall. Which ElastiCache capabilities meet these needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Compatibility with Redis OSS, Valkey and Memcached
options.why: Support for the common open-source caching engines lets the developers keep their existing client code, which meets the first need.

options.text: Encryption at rest and in transit through TLS
options.why: Encryption protects the cached bookings, but it neither keeps the client code working nor sizes the cache by itself.

options.text: Replicas placed in separate Availability Zones
options.why: Replicas in other zones keep the cache up through a zone outage, but they do not size the cache to demand on their own.

options.text: A serverless option that scales with demand
options.why: The serverless option grows and shrinks the cache with demand, so nobody adds or removes nodes by hand.

options.text: Reads and writes that finish in under a millisecond
options.why: Sub-millisecond speed makes pages load fast, but it neither keeps the client code nor sizes the cache on its own.

questions.takeaway: AWS Migration Hub is a free central view for planning and tracking every migration task and its progress.

read.text: Migration Hub is free and spans mobilize through migrate and modernize.

questions.stem: Leaders at a regional grocery chain want to watch the live status of every workstream of their move to AWS together. They also have no budget left for another paid tool. Which traits of AWS Migration Hub meet these two needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It adds no charge of its own to the AWS bill
options.why: Migration Hub is free, so the chain can track its move there without spending budget on the hub itself.

options.text: It shows all tasks and their progress in one central view
options.why: Migration Hub is one place to discover, assess, plan, execute and track, so leaders see all progress at once.

options.text: It gives guidance and automated recommendations
options.why: This is true of Migration Hub, but advice and recommendations do not show leaders the live status of each workstream.

options.text: It spans the mobilize phase through migrate and modernize
options.why: This is true of Migration Hub, but the phases it covers meet neither the need for a shared status view nor the budget limit.

options.text: It covers discovering, assessing and planning the move
options.why: This is true of Migration Hub, but early discovery and planning work does not give leaders live status or keep costs down.

questions.takeaway: Automated release pipelines and well-run incident response are hallmarks of the Operational Excellence pillar.

read.text: Operational Excellence: running and monitoring systems for business value, improving processes, pipeline-automated releases and good event response.

questions.stem: A mobile game studio deploys updates by hand, and missed steps keep breaking production during launches. It plans to push every release through an automated pipeline and to sharpen how staff respond to incidents. Which Well-Architected pillar does this plan address?

options.why: Reliability centers on recovering from failures and growing with demand, not on how releases are carried out.
Security is about least-privilege access and protecting data, which this release plan does not change.
Automated releases and better incident response are core parts of running systems well under Operational Excellence.
Performance Efficiency sizes resources to the workload, while the studio's problem is its manual release process.

questions.takeaway: Fast recovery of on-premises servers into an AWS Region, without a standby data center, points to Elastic Disaster Recovery.

read.text: Exact, current replicas let servers recover in the target AWS Region within minutes, with point-in-time recovery.

questions.stem: A pharmacy chain runs its prescription servers in its own data center. If that site fails, the servers must come back in an AWS Region within minutes from an up-to-date copy, and the chain wants to avoid paying for a second data center. Which service fits?

options.why: Storage Gateway extends local storage into AWS, but it does not recover whole servers in a Region.
It replicates servers to AWS continuously, so they recover in the target Region within minutes with no standby site.
Data Lifecycle Manager schedules EBS snapshots for resources already in AWS, so it cannot protect on-site servers.
Deep Archive keeps cheap long-term copies with retrieval measured in hours, far too slow for server recovery.

questions.takeaway: When an EBS volume cannot keep up, a volume type with higher IOPS raises performance without leaving EBS.

read.text: Volume types differ in price and in performance, measured in IOPS (input/output operations per second) and tied to type and often size.

questions.stem: A ticketing company runs its database on an Amazon EBS volume. At busy times checkout slows, because the volume cannot keep up with the number of reads and writes per second. The company wants to stay on Amazon EBS. What should it do?

options.text: Take snapshots of the volume more often
options.why: Snapshots back up the volume, and taking them more often adds nothing to its read and write performance.

options.text: Switch the volume to a type with higher IOPS
options.why: Volume types differ in performance measured in IOPS, and the type can be changed in place to serve more reads and writes.

options.text: Copy the volume's snapshots to a second Region
options.why: Copies in another Region help with recovery and migration, but the volume in use stays exactly as fast as before.

options.text: Turn on encryption for the volume
options.why: Encryption protects the stored data, and it does nothing to raise the number of operations the volume can serve.

questions.takeaway: Cloud migration means moving apps, databases and other IT resources into AWS from on premises or another cloud.

read.text: Moving apps, databases and other IT resources from on premises or another cloud to AWS.

questions.stem: Which term describes relocating applications, databases and other IT assets from a company's own data center, or from another cloud provider, into AWS?

options.why: Cloud migration is the move of IT resources from on premises or another cloud into AWS, which is what the stem describes.
A hybrid deployment keeps some resources on premises and links them to the cloud, rather than moving them across.
A multi-cloud deployment runs workloads across several cloud providers at once, rather than moving them into AWS.
Failover switches traffic to a standby resource when the primary fails, which is a recovery step rather than a move.

questions.takeaway: The Control Tower landing zone is the governed outer boundary that holds the OUs, accounts and resources under its rules.

read.text: Landing zone: the outer, best-practice multi-account boundary; every OU, account, user and resource you want under compliance rules lives inside it.

questions.stem: In AWS Control Tower, what is the landing zone?

options.text: The governed boundary holding its OUs, accounts and resources
options.why: The landing zone is the best-practice multi-account boundary that holds everything meant to follow the compliance rules.

options.text: The template that every newly created account is built from
options.why: Building each new account from one template is the work of Account Factory, a different part of Control Tower.

options.text: The high-level rules that block deployments breaking policy
options.why: Rules that block nonconforming deployments are Control Tower's controls, also called guardrails.

options.text: The visual summary of accounts, controls and compliance status
options.why: The ongoing visual summary of accounts and compliance is the Control Tower dashboard, not the landing zone.

questions.takeaway: Trusted Advisor's service limits checks warn when usage nears a limit, and many such limits can be raised.

read.text: Usage near or at a limit

questions.stem: A podcast hosting startup is about to launch many more resources and wants to know in advance whether it is nearing the caps AWS sets on how much its account may use. Which option fits?

options.why: Trusted Advisor's service limits checks flag usage that is near or at a limit, so the startup can act before a launch fails.

options.text: AWS Health's notices on service events
options.why: AWS Health reports AWS events affecting resources, and it does not compare the startup's usage with its limits.

options.text: AWS Config's results from rule evaluations
options.why: Config rules check resource settings against policies rather than how close usage is to a service limit.

options.text: CloudWatch Logs searches of app log files
options.why: CloudWatch Logs searches log files, which does not report how close the account is to its limits.

questions.takeaway: For API records that must outlast the event history window, send CloudTrail logs to Amazon S3.

read.text: The files holding events, sent to S3 or CloudWatch Logs, no 90-day cap, usable as PCI or HIPAA proof

questions.stem: A payment processor must keep a record of every API call in its AWS account for several years to support its PCI audits. Which CloudTrail feature keeps those records for that long?

options.text: CloudTrail logs delivered to Amazon S3
options.why: Log files sent to S3 have no time cap, so the processor can keep years of API records as audit proof.

options.text: CloudTrail event history in the console
options.why: Event history keeps only a rolling window of recent management events, far short of the years the audits require.
Insights flags unusual spikes in API activity, but it is no long-term store of every call made in the account.
Integrity validation shows whether delivered files were altered, but it stores nothing itself and keeps no records for years.

questions.takeaway: Tracing a threat's root cause with visual activity over time points to Amazon Detective.

read.text: After detection, it traces the root cause across your accounts.

questions.stem: After a threat alert, a nonprofit's security team wants to trace how the issue unfolded across its accounts, with charts of user and resource activity over a time window it picks. Which service fits?

options.why: Detective gathers logs and uses graph analytics to chart activity over a chosen window, tracing a threat's root cause.
GuardDuty raises threat findings, but it lacks the interactive views for tracing how an issue unfolded.
Security Hub shows posture and compliance in one view rather than deep investigation over time.
Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and does not investigate how an incident happened.

questions.takeaway: Unpredictable surges call for dynamic scaling, while known patterns suit predictive scaling.

read.text: Dynamic scaling responds to demand in real time, and predictive scaling schedules capacity ahead of expected demand.

questions.stem: A grocery delivery service gets sudden order surges that follow no schedule, such as when a storm arrives without warning. Which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling approach handles these surges?

options.why: Dynamic scaling reacts to demand as it happens, which suits surges that cannot be forecast.
Predictive scaling adds capacity ahead of expected demand, and these surges cannot be expected.
Vertical scaling makes one instance bigger and is not how Auto Scaling follows demand.
Manual changes depend on staff noticing the surge, so they cannot keep up in real time.

questions.takeaway: AWS CAF links adoption to reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency.

read.text: AWS CAF ties cloud adoption to four business outcomes: reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency.

questions.stem: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) names four outcomes that cloud adoption should deliver to an organization. Which are among those four? (Select THREE.)

options.why: Reduced business risk is one of the four business outcomes that AWS CAF ties cloud adoption to.
Increased revenue is one of the four business outcomes that AWS CAF names for cloud adoption.
Increased operational efficiency is one of the four business outcomes that AWS CAF names.
Speed and agility is a general advantage of cloud computing, but it is not one of the four outcomes AWS CAF names.
No longer guessing capacity is a general advantage of cloud computing, rather than one of the four AWS CAF outcomes.
Going global in minutes is a general advantage of cloud computing, rather than one of the four AWS CAF outcomes.

questions.takeaway: When many users arrive at once, scaling out adds parallel capacity that a bigger single server cannot.

read.text: Scaling out (horizontal): more instances share the work in parallel.

questions.stem: A bike rental shop's booking site runs on one Amazon EC2 instance and slows down on sunny weekends, when many riders book at the same moment. A more powerful server would leave each single booking just as slow as before. Which approach lets the site serve more riders at once?

options.why: Scaling out adds instances that handle bookings in parallel, so many riders are served at the same time.
Scaling up gives the one instance more power, and a faster server would not finish any booking sooner.
Scaling in removes surplus instances after a rush, which would lower capacity during the busy weekends.
Load balancing only spreads requests over existing instances, and with one instance there is nothing to spread over.

questions.takeaway: Converting text between human languages for global users is the job of Amazon Translate.

read.text: Amazon Translate: Text translation.

questions.stem: Which AWS service converts written content from one human language into another, so an application can serve users around the world?

options.why: Translate is the pre-trained service that renders text in another language for multilingual apps and documents.
Transcribe turns spoken audio into text in the same language, and it does not convert between languages.
Comprehend can detect which language a text is in and its sentiment, but it does not rewrite it in another one.
Polly speaks text aloud in many voices, yet the words stay in the language they were written in.

questions.takeaway: Combining findings from many AWS and partner tools into one view points to AWS Security Hub.

read.text: Pulls findings from AWS and partner services into one format and one view of security and compliance.

questions.stem: A hotel group receives findings from several AWS services and a partner tool, and its team wants them all in one format and one view of its compliance posture. Which service fits?

options.why: Security Hub pulls findings from AWS and partner services into one format and one view of security and compliance.
Detective digs into the root cause of one issue over time, not into a combined posture view.
GuardDuty is one source of threat findings, so it does not gather other services' findings into one place.
Firewall Manager sets firewall rules across accounts and does not combine findings from other tools.

questions.takeaway: DynamoDB needs no patching or maintenance windows, and it keeps copies in three facilities per Region for availability.

read.text: Single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, with no patching, upgrades, maintenance windows, downtime or cold starts.

questions.stem: A language-learning app keeps each learner's progress in Amazon DynamoDB, and its operations lead sets two rules. The two-person team cannot spend time keeping the database engine updated, and learner progress must stay reachable if a single data center goes offline. Which DynamoDB traits meet these rules? (Select TWO.)

options.text: AWS handles patches and upgrades with no maintenance windows
options.why: AWS keeps the engine current with no patching or maintenance windows for the team, which meets the rule about upkeep.

options.text: Encryption is applied automatically at rest and in transit
options.why: Automatic encryption protects the progress data, but it neither removes upkeep nor keeps data reachable when a data center goes offline.

options.text: Copies of the data are kept in three facilities per Region
options.why: With copies in three separate facilities, losing one data center still leaves the progress data reachable, which meets the second rule.

options.text: Throughput follows real traffic through auto scaling
options.why: Auto scaling matches capacity to demand, but it does not keep the data reachable when a data center goes offline.

options.text: Items in one table can carry different attributes
options.why: A flexible schema lets progress records differ, but it meets neither the upkeep rule nor the outage rule.

questions.takeaway: Access keys are long-term credentials for CLI and API calls, and temporary credentials from roles are preferred.

read.text: Access keys are long-term credentials, an access key ID plus a secret access key, that sign programmatic requests to the AWS CLI or API, and AWS advises temporary credentials from roles instead and never creating them for the root user.

questions.stem: Which statement describes IAM access keys?

options.text: Long-term credentials that sign CLI or API requests
options.why: An access key pairs an ID with a secret key, lasts until removed, and signs programmatic requests to the CLI or API.

options.text: Temporary credentials issued when a role is assumed
options.why: Assuming a role yields short-lived credentials, which AWS advises in place of long-term access keys.

options.text: One-time codes that a phone app shows at sign-in
options.why: A one-time code from a phone app is an MFA factor, not a credential for signing API requests.

options.text: Keys that AWS KMS uses to encrypt stored data
options.why: Encryption keys in AWS KMS lock and unlock data, while access keys authenticate programmatic calls.

questions.takeaway: Heavy, fast access to large datasets on local disks, as in a data warehouse, fits storage optimized instances.

read.text: Storage optimized: fast access to local data, as in data warehousing, large databases and I/O-heavy apps.

questions.stem: A university library runs a data warehouse whose large datasets sit on the instance's local disks. It needs fast, sustained reads and writes to those local disks. Which Amazon EC2 instance family fits best?

options.why: Storage optimized instances give fast access to local data, which suits a data warehouse on local disks.
Memory optimized instances keep data in memory, while this workload depends on local disk speed.
Accelerated computing adds GPUs and co-processors, which do not speed up local disk access.
General purpose instances balance resources and are not tuned for heavy local disk throughput.

questions.takeaway: Under consolidated billing, every member account's charges are billed through the management account.

read.text: Member account: a child account billed through the management account.

questions.stem: In an organization that uses consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, which account pays the combined bill for the charges of every account?

options.why: Member accounts are billed through the management account, which owns the organization and pays the combined bill.
Member charges roll up to the management account, so no member pays the organization's combined bill.
The root is the top container for OUs and accounts, rather than an account that receives a bill.
An OU only groups accounts, so it cannot receive or pay a bill for the organization.

questions.takeaway: Public internet traffic enters a VPC only through an attached internet gateway.

read.text: An internet gateway joins a VPC to the internet, and you must attach one before public traffic can flow in or out.

questions.stem: Which component must be attached to a VPC before anyone on the public web can reach the resources inside it?

options.why: An internet gateway is the VPC's connection to the internet, so public requests cannot enter without one.
A NAT gateway lets private instances start outbound connections and blocks ones started from the internet.
A virtual private gateway admits protected traffic from approved networks, not open requests from the public web.
A security group filters traffic for an instance, but it does not join the VPC to the internet.

questions.takeaway: Of the seven migration strategies, retain and retire leave an application where it is, while the other five move it.

read.text: Retain and retire involve no migration.

questions.stem: A company sorts every application in its portfolio into one of the seven migration strategies. Which strategies involve no migration of the application? (Select TWO.)

options.why: Retain keeps a business-critical application in its current environment for now, so it stays where it is.
Retire switches off an application that is no longer needed, so nothing moves.
Rehost moves an application to AWS as it is, so it is a migration with no changes rather than no migration.
Relocate moves virtual machines or containers that already run on premises onto a cloud host.
Replatform migrates an application with a few cloud optimizations, so the application does move.
Refactor rebuilds an application with new code and cloud-built features, the most involved migration path.

questions.takeaway: Audit Manager's prebuilt frameworks map your resources to the requirements of standards and regulations.

read.text: Prebuilt frameworks map your resources to standards and regulations.

questions.stem: Which ready-made item maps a company's AWS resources to the requirements of a standard or regulation, sparing the company the work of drawing up that mapping itself?

options.why: Audit Manager ships prebuilt frameworks that map resources to standards and regulations, so no mapping is drawn up by hand.
A Config rule checks one setting on resources, rather than mapping them to every requirement of a whole standard.

options.text: An AWS Organizations service control policy
options.why: A service control policy caps permissions for accounts in an organization and maps nothing to a regulation.
An Artifact agreement is a contract with AWS, which holds no mapping of the company's resources to a standard.

questions.takeaway: CloudTrail log file integrity validation reveals whether delivered log files were tampered with.

read.text: Integrity validation exposes tampering, and a separate log account blocks root-level edits.

questions.stem: A car insurance company's examiner asks it to prove that its stored records of API activity stayed unchanged after AWS CloudTrail delivered them. Which CloudTrail feature shows this?

options.why: Integrity validation exposes changes made to delivered log files, so any editing of the stored records shows up.
Insights looks for unusual API volume or error rates, which is a different question from whether stored records were altered.
Event history is a searchable view of recent management events and offers no check that delivered files are unchanged.

options.text: A trail that delivers logs to Amazon S3
options.why: A trail stores the records in S3, but storing them alone gives no proof that nobody edited them after delivery.

questions.takeaway: For who changed what, when and from where in an AWS account, look to the API call records in CloudTrail.

read.text: Who called, when, from which IP, and the result: a new state or a denial.

questions.stem: A credit union finds that the access settings on one of its storage buckets changed over the weekend. Its security lead must find out which identity made the change, when it happened and from which IP address. Which service answers this?

options.why: CloudTrail records each API call with the caller, the time, the source IP and the result, which answers all three questions.
CloudWatch tracks performance metrics and alarms, which shows how resources behave but names no caller behind a change.
Trusted Advisor might flag a bucket that is open too widely, but it keeps no record of who changed the settings or when.
Artifact hands out AWS's own audit reports and agreements, which hold nothing about activity inside the credit union's account.

questions.takeaway: Giving one instance more CPU or memory is vertical scaling, also called scaling up.

read.text: Scaling up (vertical): give running instances more power.

questions.stem: What is it called when a running Amazon EC2 instance is changed to a larger size with more CPU and memory?

options.why: Giving one existing instance more CPU and memory is vertical scaling, also called scaling up.
Scaling out adds more instances to share the work rather than making one instance bigger.
Scaling in removes surplus instances after demand falls, which is the opposite of adding power.
Load balancing spreads requests across instances and never changes the size of any instance.

questions.takeaway: S3 One Zone-IA trades multi-zone resilience for a lower price on infrequently accessed, easily recreated data.

read.text: S3 One Zone-IA: one Availability Zone instead of Standard-IA's three, so cheaper, for secondary backups or easily recreated data without high availability needs.

questions.stem: Which Amazon S3 storage class keeps infrequently accessed data in a single Availability Zone at a lower price than S3 Standard-IA?

options.why: Express One Zone is also single-zone, but it is built for the hottest, most latency-sensitive data.
Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers by usage, and it is chosen for unknown access patterns.
Glacier Instant Retrieval is an archive class for rarely read data, chosen for archives rather than for a single zone.
One Zone-IA keeps infrequent-access data in one zone instead of three, which lowers its price.

questions.takeaway: A homogeneous migration keeps the same database engine on both ends, which makes it fairly simple.

read.text: Homogeneous: the same engine on both ends, so fairly simple.

questions.stem: Why is a homogeneous database migration usually fairly simple?

options.text: The source and target run the same engine
options.why: A homogeneous migration keeps the same engine on both ends, so no schema or code conversion is needed.

options.text: AWS SCT rewrites the schema for a new engine
options.why: Schema rewriting with AWS SCT serves heterogeneous moves to a different engine, the opposite case.

options.text: The data travels to AWS on a physical device
options.why: Shipping data on a device is offline transfer, which says nothing about whether the engines match.

options.text: The application is rebuilt with new code first
options.why: Rebuilding the application with new code is the refactor strategy, which adds work rather than making the move simpler.

questions.takeaway: Short-lived access to one private object, with the bucket policy left alone, calls for an S3 presigned URL.

read.text: Presigned URLs grant expiring access without touching the bucket policy.

questions.stem: A small publishing house keeps manuscripts in a private Amazon S3 bucket. It wants a freelance editor to download one manuscript over the next few days, without editing the bucket policy. What should it do?

options.text: Generate a presigned URL for the object
options.why: A presigned URL gives the editor time-limited access to that one object and leaves the bucket policy unchanged.

options.text: Turn off S3 Block Public Access for the bucket
options.why: Lifting the block would still need a public policy and would expose far more than a single manuscript.

options.text: Add the editor as a principal in the bucket policy
options.why: This edits the bucket policy, which the publishing house wants to leave alone.

options.text: Switch on static website hosting for the bucket
options.why: Website hosting does not open private objects to anyone, and it would not limit access to a few days.

questions.takeaway: Amazon ECS is AWS's own streamlined container orchestrator, distinct from Kubernetes-based EKS.

read.text: ECS is the streamlined, integrated orchestrator, for Docker containers and others.

questions.stem: Which AWS service is a streamlined container orchestrator built by AWS, which deploys and scales containers once a team sets the images and resources such as load balancers?

options.why: ECS is AWS's own integrated orchestrator, and it manages containers once the images and resources are set.
EKS orchestrates containers by running Kubernetes, the open source platform, rather than AWS's own orchestrator.
ECR is a registry that stores container images, and it does not deploy or scale containers.
Fargate is serverless compute that containers run on, while an orchestrator decides what runs there.

questions.takeaway: Skill and process gaps found across the AWS CAF perspectives feed the AWS CAF Action Plan, which guides change management.

read.text: Skill and process gaps found per perspective feed the AWS CAF Action Plan, which guides change management.

questions.stem: A home goods importer reviews its cloud readiness one perspective at a time, from Business and People through Security and Operations, and finds gaps in skills and processes. What do those gaps feed into to guide its change management?

options.why: Gaps found per perspective feed the AWS CAF Action Plan, which steers change management for the move.
The Well-Architected Tool reviews workloads against best practices, rather than collecting AWS CAF skill gaps.
Trusted Advisor checks an account for cost, security and performance issues, rather than planning organizational change.
The Pricing Calculator estimates service costs and plays no part in tracking skill and process gaps.

questions.takeaway: Scalability is planned, long-term growth by adding resources, unlike elasticity's automatic real-time changes.

read.text: Scalability looks ahead: long-term capacity planning so a system can absorb more users or work by adding resources.

questions.stem: Which cloud concept is about planning ahead so that a system can grow to handle more users and more work as resources are added over time?

options.why: Scalability is the long-term ability to take on more load by adding resources, which is what the stem describes.
Elasticity is the automatic, moment-to-moment growing and shrinking of resources, not long-term planning.
High availability is about staying in service without a single point of failure, not about growth.
Fault tolerance is about continuing to work when a part fails, not about planning for more users.

questions.takeaway: An AWS Region is a geographic area chosen near customers, and each one contains three or more Availability Zones.

read.text: AWS Region: a geographic area with three or more AZs.

questions.stem: Which component of the AWS global infrastructure is a geographic area, chosen near customers, that groups several isolated locations?

options.why: An edge location is a small site that caches content near users, and it holds no Availability Zones.
A data center is a single facility inside an Availability Zone, so it sits below the AZ rather than above it.
A Region is a geographic area near customers made up of three or more isolated Availability Zones.
An Availability Zone is one of the isolated locations inside a Region, rather than the area that groups them.
